column1: # THE BERLIN MARRIAGE INDEXES ARE FREE AND UNSEARCHABLE, AND SEVERAL ROWS HAVE BEEN COSTING THEM WRONG.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. At least three open work list rows propose, as their CHEAPEST NEXT TEST, a
# search of the Berlin marriage name-indexes — row 242 for a LEIBHOLZ–NETTER marriage, row 254 for a
# LEIBHOLZ–SCHÖNFELD one, row 257 for a Leibholz marrying a Protestant wife. All three call it free.
# IT IS FREE. IT IS ALSO IMAGE-ONLY, AND THAT MAKES IT EXPENSIVE.
*** FOUR MARRIAGE VOLUMES SAMPLED ACROSS TWO OFFICES AND THREE DECADES. ALL FOUR SCORE 0.0. ***
column2: Schöneberg 1940-41 (P Rep. 163 Nr. 1064, 338 pp) · Schöneberg 1942-43 (Nr. 1377, 317 pp) · Charlottenburg I 1916-20 (Nr. 466, 382 pp) · Charlottenburg I 1935-38 (Nr. 566, 171 pp). THE CONTROL COUNTS SIX COMMON SURNAMES PER PAGE AND FOUND NONE AT ALL — not a thin layer, NO EXTRACTABLE TEXT WHATEVER.

Enumerated office by office across the whole of LABSA: *** MARRIAGE INDEXES, 313 VOLUMES, 28.3 GB, LATEST YEAR 1944. *** (Births: 209 volumes, 14.8 GB, latest year 1914. Deaths run to 1994, which is why the death sweeps worked.)

column1: *** SO THE REAL COST OF A BERLIN MARRIAGE SEARCH IS NOT A DOWNLOAD, IT IS AN EYE ***
column2: at the four to six image reads a volume this archive's method costs, a surname with no borough and no year is on the order of FIFTEEN HUNDRED READS. A search with a known office and a five-year window is perhaps twenty-five reads and entirely reasonable. THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT UNUSABLE; IT IS UNUSABLE UNSCOPED.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THAT DOES TO THE ROWS THAT LEAN ON IT ----------------
ROW 242, WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ × NANETTE NÉE NETTER
column2: the row calls the marriage index its cheapest test. IT IS NOT CHEAP, BUT IT IS THE BEST SCOPED OF THE THREE: William is traced in the directories to Charlottenburg and then Grunewald/Wilmersdorf 1920-1933, and Joachim Peter was born in 1903 — so the marriage is BEFORE 1903 and the office is Berlin or Charlottenburg. That is a real window, and it is the one marriage search in the archive worth running by eye.

column1: ROW 254, THE LEIBHOLZ WOMAN WHO MARRIED SCHÖNFELD
column2: the row already found, on 23 September, that the indexes stop at 1944 and that a woman widowed by 1982 may well have married after 1945 — so the free route "settles it if the marriage is pre-1945 and CANNOT TOUCH IT otherwise". THAT STANDS AND IS NOW WORSE: even inside the reachable years it is an image job with no office and no year.

the row itself already began to doubt the word "free" — its last line reads "TEST (2) COSTED AT THE IMAGE, AND THE WORD 'FREE' IN THIS ROW IS DOING TOO MUCH WORK". THIS FILE FINISHES THAT SENTENCE WITH A NUMBER: zero extractable text, 313 volumes, no narrowing available for a man whose age, address and parents are all unknown.

column1: # ---------------- THE GENERAL RULE, WHICH IS THE POINT ----------------
*** "FREE" AND "SEARCHABLE" ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN CONFLATING THEM ***
column2: Every LABSA volume is free to anyone with a browser. That says nothing about whether a name can be FOUND in it. The death indexes are searchable from about 1970 because the registers were typed; the marriage indexes are not searchable at all because they never were. A row that says "free" when it means "downloadable" will keep proposing work nobody can do.

column1: the test to run before proposing any LABSA search, and it costs one volume
column2: download one volume of the series and year in question and score its text layer against six common surnames. Below about 0.15 a page the series is image-only and the row must be scoped to an office and a window before it is worth anything. The scanner does this automatically and refuses to call anything a negative below the floor.
